```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(broom)
```

```{r import data}
# Import the data from the specified path
youth_not_eet <- read.csv("/Users/vasilikimichalia/Desktop/IDS_Group_Proj-main/Exported_data/youth_not_in_eet.csv")
# Rename the fourth column for clarity
colnames(youth_not_eet)[4] <- "Percentage"
```
```{r}
# 1. Define youth_summary and continent_colors
# Calculate the weighted average data
youth_summary <- youth_not_eet %>%
  group_by(Continent, Year) %>%
  # Use na.rm = TRUE in weighted.mean to handle missing data
  summarise(weighted_average = weighted.mean(Percentage, Population, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()

# Define the color mapping vector
continent_colors <- c(
  "Africa"        = "#F8766D",
  "Asia"          = "#B79F00",
  "Europe"        = "#00BA38",
  "North America" = "#00BFC4",
  "Oceania"       = "#619CFF",
  "South America" = "#F564E3"
)
# 1. Calculate all slopes, p-values, and annotation positions
slope_data <- youth_summary %>%
  # Group the data by continent so that the linear model is fitted separately for each group
  group_by(Continent) %>%
  # Use 'do' to perform a non-standard evaluation (fitting the model) on each group
  do({
    # Fit the linear model (Ordinary Least Squares) where weighted_average is the outcome
    # and Year is the predictor variable.
    lm_fit <- lm(weighted_average ~ Year, data = .)
    
    # Use 'tidy' from the 'broom' package to neatly extract model coefficients and statistics
    tidy_fit <- broom::tidy(lm_fit)
    
    # Get the row corresponding to the 'Year' term (which contains the slope and p-value)
    slope_stats <- tidy_fit %>% filter(term == "Year")
    
    # Extract the slope estimate (coefficient for the Year variable)
    slope <- slope_stats$estimate
    # Extract the p-value associated with the slope (to test H0: slope = 0)
    p_value <- slope_stats$p.value
    
    # Determine the significance notation based on standard alpha levels (0.05, 0.01, 0.001)
    significance_label <- case_when(
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "(p < 0.001)", # Highly significant
      p_value < 0.01 ~ "(p < 0.01)",     # Very significant
      p_value < 0.05 ~ "(p < 0.05)",      # Significant at the 5% level
      TRUE ~ " (n.s.)"                      # Not significant (p >= 0.05)
    )
    
    # Create the final annotation label string, including the formatted slope and significance
    slope_label <- sprintf("Slope: %s%.3f %s",
                           ifelse(slope >= 0, "+", ""), # Add a '+' sign for positive slopes
                           slope,
                           significance_label)
    
    # Return a new data frame with the label and continent (no x/y needed for this method)
    data.frame(
      Continent = unique(.$Continent),
      slope_label = slope_label
    )
  }) %>%
  # Ungroup the data to allow it to be used in the ggplot call later
  ungroup()

# Section 2: Combined Plot Generation

# 2. Create the combined plot using facet_wrap
# Start the ggplot object, using the full summary data and mapping Year/Percentage to axes
combined_plot <- ggplot(youth_summary, aes(x = Year, y = weighted_average)) +
  
  # Add point geom, mapping the point color to the 'Continent' variable
  geom_point(aes(colour = Continent), alpha = 0.7, size = 3) +
  
  # Add smoothing line (linear model, show standard error), mapping color/fill to 'Continent'
  geom_smooth(aes(colour = Continent, fill = Continent), method = "lm", se = TRUE, size = 1) +
  
  # Add the slope text annotations using the pre-calculated 'slope_data'
  geom_text(data = slope_data,
            # Place annotation in the top-left corner inside each facet
            aes(label = slope_label, colour = Continent),
            x = -Inf, y = Inf,
            hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2,
            size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  
  # Apply the custom hexadecimal color codes to the 'colour' aesthetic
  scale_colour_manual(values = continent_colors) +
  # Apply the custom hexadecimal color codes to the 'fill' aesthetic (for confidence interval)
  scale_fill_manual(values = continent_colors) +
  
  # Split the single plot into multiple panels based on the 'Continent' variable
  facet_wrap(~ Continent,
             # 'free_y' allows each panel to have its own vertical axis range for better visualization
             scales = "free_y") +
  
  # Define the plot labels (axes and title)
  labs( x = "Year",
        y = "Weighted Average Percentage",
        # Use \n for a line break in the title and define the significance notation
        title = "Youth Not in EET: Trend by Continent\n(* = significant at 5% level)") +
  
  # Apply a minimalist theme
  theme_minimal() +
  # Customize theme elements
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, hjust = 0), # Title text size and left-alignment
    legend.position = "none",                        # Hide the legend as colors are continent-specific in facets
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold") # Format the facet panel labels (Continent names)
  )

# Display the final combined plot object
combined_plot

```
